narr: Strong heating during the afternoon created an unstable airmass with surface-based CAPE values in excess of 3,000 J/Kg across Tazewell County and the surrounding area, while precipitable water values varied between 1.6 and 1.8 inches. One thunderstorm developed to the near Richlands at around 6:15 pm EDT and lingered for about 75 minutes before weakening. This storm produced prolonged rainfall rates of 3 to 4 inches per hour. Runoff from this storm resulted in small stream flooding of tributaries of the Clinch River, including Little Town Hill Creek, which flooded across U.S. Highway 460 and Hillcreek Road. MRMS FLASH (Flooded Locations and Simulated Hydrograph) data indicated a 3-hour Average Recurrence Interval between a 40- and 75-year event, while estimated rainfall was up to 1.8 times that of 3-hour flash flood guidance. CREST (Coupled Routing and Excess Storage) Unit Streamflow in the area ranged from 300 to 500 cfs per square mile.
ev: Heavy rain caused Little Town Hill Creek to overflow its banks, flooding across Hillcreek Road, as well as U.S. Highway 460 to a depth of up to 4 feet. One car was caught in the floodwater and the occupant had to be rescued by emergency responders. Flooding across Highway 460 lasted for around two hours before flooding receded and the highway was reopened. No damage to the road was reported, but with some damage to the flooded vehicle.
Minor flooding was reported along Burnette Street when a tributary of the Clinch River was observed overflowing its banks onto Burnette Street. No damage was reported.
lsr: LITTLE TOWN HILL CREEK OVERFLOWED ITS BANKS WITH FLOODING ACROSS HILL CREEK ROAD.
